title: Training Volume and Training Frequency Changes Associated with Boston Marathon Race Performance
authors: DeJong Lempke A, Ackerman K, Stellingwerff T, Burke L, Baggish A, d'Hemecourt P, Dyer S, Troyanos C
population: 917 adult registrants of the 2022 Boston Marathon (495 women, finish 3:53 +/- 0:37 h, 64.4 +/- 24 km/week; 422 men, 3:35 +/- 0:39 h, 67.6 +/- 26.2 km/week), surveyed one month before the race.
findings: Runners reported training one month before the race; training in the 12-4 months and the 4-0 months before the race, and the change between the two (training frequency changes), were related to chip time in linear regressions that accounted for experience and demographics.

Higher running distance a week, more running sessions a week, more quality (hard) sessions a week and higher average distance, in both periods, were associated with faster times (p <= 0.050), as was more cross-training in the 4-0 months before the race (p < 0.001).
Runners whose running sessions a week decreased between the two periods had faster times and better performance than those who maintained or increased.
The authors conclude that habitually higher training exposure over 12-4 and 4-0 months, with a relatively reduced training frequency in the last 4 months, contributed to better marathon performance.
limitations: Self-reported training and a cross-sectional design: an association, not an effect, and the runners who train more are different runners. Registrants of one major marathon are a self-selected group. The abstract reports that volume was higher in faster runners and gives no curve, plateau or ceiling. The change in frequency in the last 4 months mixes a taper with other causes. Abstract read; full text not read.
implications: Adds a 917-runner cross-sectional association of weekly distance, sessions and quality sessions held over the year before a marathon with faster times: volume is higher in faster runners across the range reported (about 64-68 km/week on average), as the earlier cohorts found. It is between-runner and cannot set a ceiling for one runner.
A fall in sessions a week in the last 4 months went with better times, which fits a taper and does not speak to the weeks of a plateau.
